source_phrase: Typical symptoms induced by RGSV infection are leaf yellowing (chlorosis), stunting, and excess tillering (branching) (Shikata et al., 1980)

note: Pronounced dwarfing and stunting diagnostic of RGSV

source_phrase: Chlorosis and stunting are also observed in plants infected with other tenuiviruses, whereas excess tillering is a symptom specific to RGSV infection.
citation: Satoh, K., Yoneyama, K., Kondoh, H., Shimizu, T., Sasaya, T., Choi, I.R., Yoneyama, K., Omura, T. & Kikuchi, S. (2013). Relationship between gene responses and symptoms induced by Rice grassy stunt virus. Frontiers in Microbiology, 4, 313.

source_phrase: RGSV is a member of the genus Tenuivirus, and is transmitted by brown planthopper (BPH, Nilaparvata lugens) and by two other Nilaparvata spp
citation: Satoh, K., Yoneyama, K., Kondoh, H., Shimizu, T., Sasaya, T., Choi, I.R., Yoneyama, K., Omura, T. & Kikuchi, S. (2013). Relationship between gene responses and symptoms induced by Rice grassy stunt virus. Frontiers in Microbiology, 4, 313.
note: Obligate insect vector Nilaparvata lugens
